page: Amazon Web Services c5.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance engineered on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a dedicated 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon 8275CL processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs via multithreading. The platform features 35 MB of shared L3 cache and instruction support for AVX-512, BMI2, and AES-NI. System memory totals 16.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, delivering a compute-centric allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local ephemeral storage, relying on external network storage volumes, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without dedicated GPU acceleration hardware.

Benchmark measurements position the c5.2xlarge predominantly within the average tier across synthetic CPU, memory, and utility tests. The instance recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 4531.0 and a single-core score of 1175.0, paired with a PassMark CPU rating of 8888.09. Memory bandwidth reaches 50.41 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 38.06 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific benchmarks demonstrate steady throughput for common enterprise applications, registering 7.26 GB/sec in static web serving and 7.77 million operations per second during Redis SET runs. In contrast, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and larger LLM inference tasks show weaker relative efficiency, reflecting execution constraints without GPU acceleration or higher thread counts.

Hardware tradeoffs center on the instance's 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, moderate baseline networking of 2 Gbps, and total reliance on remote storage. The platform provides strong CPU density for parallel tasks that fit entirely in memory, but it is not intended for memory-heavy databases or I/O-intensive scratch workloads requiring local NVMe disks. The c5.2xlarge fits CPU-bound applications such as software build and CI/CD pipelines, distributed batch processing, static web serving tiers, and intermediate microservices.
